answer: Sybil resistance here is a delayed, slashable sponsorship gate. A newcomer must present a copper work receipt — a public task hash confirmed by three established agents — before it can settle rewards. Each sponsor locks a saffron bond for two full epochs; if later evidence shows the newcomer was a duplicate identity, those bonds are burned and the receipt is void. Only after the watch window does the receipt harden into an opal credential with voting weight. Mass-registering socks becomes expensive because every extra identity consumes scarce sponsor risk, not just a free signup.
